title: Account Runway Allocator and Customer Concordance Policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We currently field a high volume of escalations and VIP asks that compete with our sprint capacity and roadmap commitments. Ad-hoc allocation creates uncertainty for engineering and poor expectation setting for customers.

Goal: Define an operational policy and lightweight scoring algorithm (Account Runway Allocator) that converts customer signals into deterministic sprint slot allocations and escalation paths. The policy should be transparent to stakeholders, automatable in our intake UI, and produce metrics we can track in the Console.

Scope: Top-account requests (enterprise customers with committed contracts or renewal within 6 months) and time-sensitive escalations that require an explicit roadmap decision. This policy will not replace ad-hoc bugs/security hotfixes or small-scope bugfix requests under 2 points.

Core components: 1) Signal harmonization: combine contract value, renewal proximity, incident severity, customer advocacy level, technical feasibility estimate, and opportunity-to-revenue multiplier into a single concordance score. 2) Runway allocation: map score bands to sprint slot types (Immediate Escalation slot, Fastpass 1 sprint, Fastpass 2-2 sprints, Queue). 3) Guardrails: caps per cycle, transparent fallback promises, and escalation owners. 4) Telemetry: dashboards for booking velocity, SLA adherence for top accounts, and forecasted capacity impact.

Algorithm (high-level): 1. Normalize signals to 0-100 each. 2. Apply weights: ContractValue(30), RenewalWindow(20), IncidentSeverity(20), Advocacy(15), FeasibilityCost(10, inverse), StrategicMultiplier(5). 3. ConcordanceScore = weighted sum. 4. Apply hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping between bands across cycles. 5. Tie band to automated sprint slot recommendation and a human approval step for P1 decisions.

Why different from existing frameworks: Rather than manual VIP lanes or ad-hoc fast-tracking, this policy formalizes the conversion of disparate customer signals into deterministic capacity allocations and explicit fallout SLAs, enabling predictability for Eng and PM while preserving negotiation levers for Sales/Customer Success.
acceptance_criteria: Concordance scoring prototype documented and validated on 10 historical top-account requests with retrospective score vs outcome.
UI intake widget mocks created for Console that display score, recommended slot, and required approver.
Rollout playbook written: owner roles, approver matrix, cap enforcement, and fallback messaging templates.
Telemetry dashboard panels in Console showing bookings-by-band, SLA compliance, and forecasted cycle capacity impact.
Pilot run with two sales-managed accounts during cycle 2026-W12 with retrospective learnings captured.
metrics: % of top-account asks assigned to a slot within 48 hours
Cycle-level capacity consumed by allocated slots (story points and % of sprint capacity)
SLA adherence for Immediate Escalation (time to triage, time to ship workaround)
Conversion rate of allocated slots into shipped roadmap items within committed window
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Design): finalize weights and scoring with Sales, CS, and Eng; mock intake UI. Phase 2 (Pilot): enable scoring as a recommendation flag in the intake form for a 2-cycle pilot with guardrail caps. Phase 3 (Automate): enforce slot caps in ticketing and expose dashboards; train approvers. Phase 4 (Scale): roll to all top-account intake and embed into quarterly intake cadence.
risks: Over-weighting revenue signals could bias toward high-revenue but low-strategic-fit asks
Engineering capacity pressure if caps are set too permissive
Stakeholder pushback from Accounts used to subjective fast-tracking
Score gaming risk if Sales/CS artificially inflate advocacy or feasibility estimates
implementation_notes: ENG work items required: 1) intake API hook to compute concordance score (frontend + backend), 2) Console intake UI updates, 3) dashboard panels (bookings and capacity), 4) enforcement middleware that flags when cycle caps exceeded. We should reuse existing intake forms and issues workflow where possible to minimize UI churn. Prototype code will live in gh:redwood/roadmap-intake under a feature branch PM/allocator-prototype.
